page: Microsoft Azure E8ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the processor includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_ni. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

This server includes 307 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark testing, the E8ds_v5 demonstrates solid memory performance, achieving a read-only small block cached memory bandwidth of 417.0 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 44.14 GB/sec. CPU performance is characterized by a Geekbench multi-core score of 6145.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 11541.37. The local storage and memory architecture support high-throughput operations, as evidenced by a Redis SET performance of 7.88 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 12.5 GB/sec.

While the instance performs well in memory-intensive tasks, it exhibits limitations in heavy computational workloads such as large-scale machine learning. LLM inference benchmarks show weak performance on a medium 7B model, processing prompts at 17.36 tokens per second and generating text at 6.39 tokens per second. Consequently, the E8ds_v5 is highly cost-efficient for memory-bound applications, relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring high memory density per core, but is less suitable for intensive AI or GPU-accelerated workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E8ds_v5 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating at 2.8 GHz, it features 48 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 instruction sets. The server includes 307 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. Benchmark results indicate balanced performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6145.0, a Redis SET throughput of 7.88 million operations per second, and a static web serving throughput of 12.5 GB/sec. However, LLM inference performance on a 7B model is weak, generating 6.39 tokens per second. This instance is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching layers, offering a robust qualitative balance of high memory density and local SSD storage without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware.
